text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's new parliament elected the leader of the Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) Ivan Kostov as prime minister, following his coalition's victory in April 19 general elections.

Parliament also approved Kostov's cabinet lineup and programme. All parliamentary groups with exception of the former ruling Socialists gave their support for the new government to carry out vital reforms to end crisis.
-- Bistra Dimitrova, chairman of Bulgaria's largest savings institution, the State Savings Bank, said she would resign by the end of the week, the government press centre said.

-- Bulgaria's new government has to win the war against poverty, corruption and crime, against inflation and for restoring Bulgarians' self-esteem, President Petar Stoyanov told parliament after election of the new cabinet.

-- The Socialist deputies in parliament declined to support the UDF cabinet, saying its programme included good intentions and ideas but no clear decisions, Georgi Pirinski, former Socialist foreign minister, told parliament.
-- Bulgaria's former Interim Prime minister Stefan Sofianski resumed his duties as a mayor of Sofia after the new UDF government headed by Ivan Kostov was sworn in.
-- Bulgaria has sold 25 trade firms and has open procedures for the sale of another 100 during the 99-day term of office of the interim cabinet, former interim trade minister Daniela Bobeva said.
-- The central bank might decide to cut its main interest rate to fall to around 3.7 percent monthly from the current 4.3 percent from next week, the newspaper quoted dealers as saying.
